literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 羟基自由基使游离 MNV-1 和囊泡隐形 MNV-1 失活,其二级速率常数约为 1010 M-1 s-1,但囊泡膜提供了 2.24 倍的保护作用,导致隐形 MNV-1 的失活动力学较慢。 [10.1021/acs.est.6c05945]

与 EE 相比,超声 治疗 与更高的总酚含量(约 2.2 至 3.8 倍)和抗氧化能力(约 1.9 至 2.3 倍)相关。对于 MNV,过夜暴露后,S. trojana-EE 的最大减少量为 2.42 log 10 TCID 50 /mL。抑制区直径范围为 6.25 至 11.75 mm,包括 6 mm 圆盘。在测试条件下,FRhK-4 的存活率约为 56% 至 100%,排除了低细胞毒性的普遍说法。 [10.1007/s12560-026-09709-y]
与经过认证的临床 RT-qPCR 试剂盒相比,GII.3、GII.4 和 GII.17 的总一致性百分比分别为 98.7%、99.3% 和 96.9%,并且阈值时间具有显着的线性相关性。至关重要的是,与 RT-qPCR 相比,Lab-CPA 系统将处理时间缩短了 44-60 分钟。 [10.1128/spectrum.01684-26]
倾向得分匹配产生了 178 个平衡良好的对,所有五个协变量都实现了标准化平均差 (SMD)。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10484333/v1]
提供的证据没有明确说明直接观察到的主要结果。 [10.3791/24133]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Hydroxyl radicals inactivated both free MNV-1 and vesicle-cloaked MNV-1 with second rate constants of ∼1010 M-1 s-1, but the vesicle membrane provided a 2.24-fold protective effect, resulting in slower inactivation kinetics for cloaked MNV-1. [10.1021/acs.est.6c05945]

Ultrasound treatment was associated with higher measured total phenolic content (approximately 2.2- to 3.8-fold) and antioxidant capacity (approximately 1.9- to 2.3-fold) than EE. For MNV, the largest reduction was 2.42 log 10 TCID 50 /mL for S. trojana-EE after overnight exposure. [10.1007/s12560-026-09709-y]

Compared to certified clinical RT-qPCR kits, the total percent agreement was 98.7%, 99.3%, and 96.9% for GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17, respectively, accompanied by a significant linear correlation in threshold times. Crucially, the Lab-CPA systems reduced processing time by 44–60 min compared to RT-qPCR. [10.1128/spectrum.01684-26]
Propensity score matching yielded 178 well-balanced pairs, with all five covariates achieving standardized mean difference (SMD). [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10484333/v1]
The supplied evidence does not clearly state a directly observed main result. [10.3791/24133]

literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

Hydroxyl radicals inactivated both free MNV-1 and vesicle-cloaked MNV-1 with second rate constants of ∼1010 M-1 s-1, but the vesicle membrane provided a 2.24-fold protective effect, resulting in slower inactivation kinetics for cloaked MNV-1.

papers.title: Isothermal cross-priming amplification for field-deployable norovirus surveillance: a cost-effective and rapid solution.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Norovirus remains a leading cause of foodborne gastroenteritis globally. While isothermal amplification technologies offer advantages over traditional reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) in terms of speed and portability, there is a lack of domestically developed isothermal amplification systems for norovirus in China. Using a domestic patented cross-priming amplification (CPA) technology, we established CPA systems targeting the predominant norovirus genotypes GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17. The systems were evaluated using 224 fecal samples with confirmed genotypes via sequencing. Our lab-developed CPA (Lab-CPA) systems demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting 98.0% (49/50) of GII.3, 100% (80/80) of GII.4, and 96.9% (31/32) of GII.17 samples, with 100% specificity across all genotypes. Compared to certified clinical RT-qPCR kits, the total percent agreement was 98.7%, 99.3%, and 96.9% for GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17, respectively, accompanied by a significant linear correlation in threshold times. Crucially, the Lab-CPA systems reduced processing time by 44–60 min compared to RT-qPCR. Successful integration into the commercial EasyNAT platform using all-in-one cartridges further streamlined the workflow while maintaining accuracy. Our CPA systems offer a rapid, cost-effective, and streamlined diagnostic solution, ideally suited for point-of-care testing in resource-limited primary healthcare environments. IMPORTANCE Norovirus remains a critical public health threat, driving demand for rapid, deployable diagnostics. While isothermal amplification offers theoretical advantages over reverse transcription quantitative PCR, the absence of domestically developed systems in China has created a reliance on imported assays, limiting point-of-care testing capabilities. This study addresses that gap by establishing a novel cross-priming amplification system tailored to China’s predominant norovirus genotypes. Achieving high sensitivity/specificity and significantly reducing processing time, this work validates a robust, field-adaptable alternative to conventional methods. Furthermore, successful integration with the commercial EasyNAT platform demonstrates immediate translational potential. By providing a cost-effective, high-performance domestic solution, these findings significantly enhance decentralized surveillance and emergency response capacity for norovirus infections in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Treated Ethanolic Extracts of Endemic Mount Ida Plants (Sideritis trojana and Hypericum kazdaghensis) Show Antiviral and Antibacterial Potential Against Norovirus Surrogates and Foodborne Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Human noroviruses and persistent bacterial pathogens remain major food-safety concerns. This screening study compared 40% (v/v) ethanolic extracts (EE) and ultrasound-treated ethanolic extracts (UTE) of the endemic Mount Ida plants Sideritis trojana Ehrend. and Hypericum kazdaghensis Gemici & Leblebici. Feline calicivirus (FCV) and murine norovirus (MNV) served as cultivable human-norovirus surrogates; four reference bacteria were examined by disc diffusion. Ultrasound treatment was associated with higher measured total phenolic content (approximately 2.2- to 3.8-fold) and antioxidant capacity (approximately 1.9- to 2.3-fold) than EE. The largest reduction was 4.71 log 10 TCID 50 /mL for H. kazdaghensis-UTE against FCV after overnight exposure. For MNV, the largest reduction was 2.42 log 10 TCID 50 /mL for S. trojana-EE after overnight exposure. Inhibition-zone diameters ranged from 6.25 to 11.75 mm, including the 6-mm disc. FRhK-4 viability ranged from approximately 56% to 100% across the tested conditions, precluding a general claim of low cytotoxicity. The results provide preliminary, surrogate- and assay-specific evidence of antiviral and antibacterial activity. Because solvent-only and positive controls were not included, causal attribution to plant constituents and comparison with established antimicrobials are not possible. Confirmatory controlled assays are required before practical food-safety use can be proposed.

papers.title: Hydroxyl Radical Inactivation of Vesicle-Cloaked and Free Murine Norovirus: Linking Biomolecular Oxidation to Lifecycle Disruption and Infectivity Loss.
papers.abstract: Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) play a central role in inactivating human viruses during advanced oxidation processes for water and wastewater treatment, solar disinfection, and natural attenuation in sunlit aquatic environments. Human norovirus, a leading cause of gastroenteritis, is efficiently transmitted through water and exhibits strong environmental persistence. The recent discovery of vesicle-cloaked virus clusters (viral vesicles) further challenges water treatment and reuse, particularly for norovirus elimination. We investigated •OH inactivation kinetics and mechanisms of murine norovirus 1 (MNV-1), a human norovirus surrogate, in free-virus and vesicle-cloaked forms. •OH rapidly inactivated both MNV-1 vesicles and free MNV-1 with second rate constants of ∼1010 M-1 s-1; however, the vesicle membrane provided a 2.24-fold protective effect to cloaked MNV-1, resulting in slower inactivation kinetics than those of free MNV-1. •OH oxidized viral capsid proteins and genomes together with vesicle proteins and lipids, resulting in impaired CD300lf receptor and cell-based binding, disrupted genome replication, and diminished viral assembly. Despite these biochemical and functional impairments, most vesicle structures remained largely intact following •OH exposure. This study establishes a quantitative framework linking biomolecular damage to viral infectivity loss through functional impairment and lifecycle disruption, providing mechanistic insights into advance water disinfection strategies and public health protection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the inactivation kinetics and mechanisms of murine norovirus 1 (MNV-1), a surrogate for human norovirus, by hydroxyl radicals (•OH) in both free-virus and vesicle-cloaked forms, addressing the challenge of effective virus elimination in water treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using murine norovirus 1 (MNV-1) as the target virus, with comparisons made between free-virus and vesicle-cloaked forms. The research focused on the inactivation of MNV-1 by hydroxyl radicals in controlled experimental settings.
analysis.methods: The study employed hydroxyl radical inactivation experiments on MNV-1 in both free and vesicle-cloaked forms, measuring the rate constants and assessing the impact on viral capsid proteins, genomes, and vesicle structures through biochemical and functional analyses.
analysis.main_results: Hydroxyl radicals inactivated both free MNV-1 and vesicle-cloaked MNV-1 with second rate constants of ∼1010 M-1 s-1, but the vesicle membrane provided a 2.24-fold protective effect, resulting in slower inactivation kinetics for cloaked MNV-1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that hydroxyl radicals cause oxidative damage to both viral capsid proteins and genomes, as well as vesicle proteins and lipids, leading to impaired receptor binding, disrupted genome replication, and diminished viral assembly, which is a novel mechanistic insight into viral inactivation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights into the effectiveness of hydroxyl radical-based water disinfection strategies for reducing norovirus infectivity, which can inform public health measures and water treatment protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to MNV-1, a surrogate for human norovirus, and does not account for variations in human norovirus strains or environmental factors, resulting in moderate confidence in the generalizability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the inactivation of murine norovirus 1 (MNV-1) by hydroxyl radicals (•OH) in both free-virus and vesicle-cloaked forms. It highlights the protective effect of the vesicle membrane, which slows inactivation kinetics compared to free MNV-1. The research demonstrates that •OH causes oxidative damage to viral components, impairing receptor binding, genome replication, and viral assembly. papers.title_zh: 囊泡包裹和游离小鼠 诺如病毒 的羟基自由基失活:将生物分子氧化与生命周期破坏和感染性丧失联系起来。
papers.source_body_en: Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) play a central role in inactivating human viruses during advanced oxidation processes for water and wastewater treatment, solar disinfection, and natural attenuation in sunlit aquatic environments. Human norovirus, a leading cause of gastroenteritis, is efficiently transmitted through water and exhibits strong environmental persistence. The recent discovery of vesicle-cloaked virus clusters (viral vesicles) further challenges water treatment and reuse, particularly for norovirus elimination. We investigated •OH inactivation kinetics and mechanisms of murine norovirus 1 (MNV-1), a human norovirus surrogate, in free-virus and vesicle-cloaked forms. •OH rapidly inactivated both MNV-1 vesicles and free MNV-1 with second rate constants of ∼1010 M-1 s-1; however, the vesicle membrane provided a 2.24-fold protective effect to cloaked MNV-1, resulting in slower inactivation kinetics than those of free MNV-1. •OH oxidized viral capsid proteins and genomes together with vesicle proteins and lipids, resulting in impaired CD300lf receptor and cell-based binding, disrupted genome replication, and diminished viral assembly. Despite these biochemical and functional impairments, most vesicle structures remained largely intact following •OH exposure. This study establishes a quantitative framework linking biomolecular damage to viral infectivity loss through functional impairment and lifecycle disruption, providing mechanistic insights into advance water disinfection strategies and public health protection.
papers.abstract_zh: 羟基自由基 (•OH) 在水和废水 治疗 的高级氧化过程、日光消毒以及阳光照射的水生环境中的自然衰减过程中,在灭活人类病毒方面发挥着核心作用。人类 诺如病毒 是胃肠炎的主要原因,可通过水有效传播,并表现出很强的环境持久性。最近发现的囊泡病毒簇(病毒囊泡)进一步挑战了水 治疗 和再利用,特别是 诺如病毒 的消除。我们研究了鼠诺如病毒 1 (MNV-1)(人类诺如病毒 替代物)在游离病毒和囊泡包裹形式下的OH 失活动力学和机制。•OH 快速灭活 MNV-1 囊泡和游离 MNV-1,第二速率常数约为 1010 M-1 s-1;然而,囊泡膜对隐藏的 MNV-1 提供了 2.24 倍的保护作用,导致失活动力学比游离的 MNV-1 慢。•OH氧化病毒衣壳蛋白和基因组以及囊泡蛋白和脂质,导致CD300lf受体和细胞结合受损,破坏基因组复制,并减少病毒组装。尽管存在这些生化和功能损伤,大多数囊泡结构在接触·OH 后仍基本保持完整。这项研究建立了一个定量框架,通过功能损伤和生命周期破坏将生物分子损伤与病毒感染性丧失联系起来,为先进的水消毒策略和公共卫生保护提供了机制见解。

papers.title: Association between glycerin enema use and 14-day unplanned revisits in children with acute viral gastroenteritis: a dual-center retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Glycerin enema is commonly used in pediatric emergency settings to relieve fecal impaction, yet evidence on its effect on short-term outcomes in acute viral gastroenteritis remains scarce. This study examined the association between glycerin enema administered within 12 hours of initial presentation and the 14-day unplanned revisit rate in children with rotavirus- and/or norovirus-induced acute viral gastroenteritis. Methods This dual-center retrospective cohort study enrolled children aged ≤ 14 years with positive stool antigen for rotavirus and/or norovirus at Dongguan Tungwah Hospital and Dongguan Songshan Lake Tungwah Hospital from January 2021 to August 2025. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using exact matching on non-diarrhea presentation status, followed by 1∶1 nearest-neighbor matching without replacement based on standardized Euclidean distance for gender, age in months, intravenous fluid administration, and fever. The primary outcome was the 14-day unplanned revisit rate, analyzed by paired McNemar exact test. Secondary outcomes included antibiotic use, hospitalization, and symptom duration ≥ 3 days. Sensitivity analyses included Firth penalized logistic regression, exclusion of hospitalized children, and E-value assessment. Results PSM yielded 178 well-balanced pairs, with all five covariates achieving SMD

papers.title_zh: 急性病毒性胃肠炎儿童使用甘油灌肠与 14 天计划外复诊之间的关联:双中心回顾性 队列研究 研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Glycerin enema is commonly used in pediatric emergency settings to relieve fecal impaction, yet evidence on its effect on short-term outcomes in acute viral gastroenteritis remains scarce. This study examined the association between glycerin enema administered within 12 hours of initial presentation and the 14-day unplanned revisit rate in children with rotavirus- and/or norovirus-induced acute viral gastroenteritis. Methods This dual-center retrospective cohort study enrolled children aged ≤ 14 years with positive stool antigen for rotavirus and/or norovirus at Dongguan Tungwah Hospital and Dongguan Songshan Lake Tungwah Hospital from January 2021 to August 2025. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using exact matching on non-diarrhea presentation status, followed by 1∶1 nearest-neighbor matching without replacement based on standardized Euclidean distance for gender, age in months, intravenous fluid administration, and fever. The primary outcome was the 14-day unplanned revisit rate, analyzed by paired McNemar exact test. Secondary outcomes included antibiotic use, hospitalization, and symptom duration ≥ 3 days. Sensitivity analyses included Firth penalized logistic regression, exclusion of hospitalized children, and E-value assessment. Results PSM yielded 178 well-balanced pairs, with all five covariates achieving SMD
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 甘油灌肠常用于儿科急诊环境中以缓解粪便嵌塞,但其对急性病毒性胃肠炎短期结果影响的证据仍然很少。本研究探讨了轮状病毒和/或 诺如病毒 诱导的急性病毒性胃肠炎儿童初次就诊 12 小时内进行甘油灌肠与 14 天计划外复诊率之间的关系。方法双中心回顾性队列研究研究纳入2021年1月至2025年8月在东莞东华医院和东莞松山湖东华医院就诊的年龄≤14岁粪便抗原轮状病毒和/或诺如病毒阳性的儿童。采用非腹泻表现状态精确匹配进行倾向评分匹配(PSM),然后进行1∶1最近邻匹配(无腹泻)。基于性别、年龄(月数)、静脉输液和发烧的标准化欧几里得距离进行替换。主要结果是 14 天计划外重访率,通过配对 McNemar 精确检验进行分析。次要结局包括抗生素使用、住院治疗和症状持续时间≥3天。敏感性分析包括 Firth 惩罚逻辑回归、排除住院儿童和 E 值评估。结果 PSM 产生了 178 个平衡良好的对,所有五个协变量都实现了 SMD

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查急性病毒性胃肠炎儿童使用甘油灌肠与 14 天计划外复诊之间的关联,弥补其对短期结果影响的证据空白。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项双中心回顾性 队列研究 研究纳入了 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 8 月在东莞两家医院进行的 ≤ 14 岁粪便抗原轮状病毒和/或 诺如病毒 阳性的儿童。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能会为有关使用甘油灌肠治疗儿童急性病毒性胃肠炎的临床实践提供信息,并可能指导 治疗 的决策和后续策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管使用倾向评分匹配和敏感性分析加强了证据,但该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的混杂因素而受到限制。

papers.title: Epidemiological features and direct medical costs of norovirus acute gastroenteritis in China
papers.abstract: Norovirus is a leading global cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE), yet comprehensive data on its disease and economic burden across all age groups requiring medical consultation in China remains scarce, hindering evidence-based public health strategy formulation. A multi-center retrospective study was conducted on 23,527 AGE patients who underwent norovirus testing at medical institutions in four Chinese provinces between 2018 and 2024. The logistic regression models were used to analyze the related factors with norovirus infection rates, hospitalization risks, complication incidence, and direct medical costs. National annual direct medical burden of norovirus infection was estimated by combining study data with national population census and epidemiological survey data. The overall norovirus positive rate was 18.80% (95% CI 18.30%-19.30%), with a significantly higher rate in inpatients (26.15%, 95% CI 25.28%-27.04%) than outpatients (13.78%, 95% CI 13.21%-14.36%). Children < 5 years old had the highest positive rate (30.49%, 95% CI 29.56%-31.43%. A total of 18.97% (95% CI 17.84%–20.16%) of norovirus-positive patients developed at least one potential complication concurrent with norovirus-positive acute gastroenteritis, among which dehydration (11.28%, 95% CI 10.39%–12.25%) was the most prevalent, followed by convulsions (5.52%, 95% CI 4.88%–6.23%). The median direct medical costs for inpatients (CNY 4,580, IQR 3,129–6,402) was far higher than outpatients (CNY 230 IQR 128–354), with the elderly ≥ 65 years having the highest per capita direct medical costs (CNY 5,322, IQR 2,411–10,798). The national annual direct medical cost of norovirus infection was estimated at CNY 20.23 billion, with children < 5 years bearing a medical burden 11.2 times that of the elderly ≥ 60 years. papers.title: Application of VirCapSeq-VERT for viral pathogen detection in children under five with acute diarrheal illness in Zambia
papers.abstract: Diarrheal disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five years, especially in low- and middle-income countries, particularly sub-Saharan Africa. Although rotavirus vaccination has reduced burden in children, a substantial proportion of diarrhea remains unattributed due to limited diagnostic capacity. We applied VirCapSeq-VERT (VCS), a virome-wide targeted sequencing technique, to characterize viral detections and co-infection patterns in stool samples from children with diarrhea and to explore their comparison with disease severity. A cross-sectional, facility-based study across nine provincial health facilities in Zambia. Stool collected from children U5 years presenting with diarrhea was analyzed using qPCR and VCS. Positivity by VCS was defined as ≥ 25% in relation to full coding reference sequence. Severity was assessed using the Vesikari scoring system and categorized as mild or moderate-to-severe. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to evaluate viral prevalence, age-specific distribution, and co-infection patterns. Samples from 247 participants were analyzed by VCS with 48.6% aged 0–12 months; males accounting for 52.6%. Using VCS to interrogate the stool samples, rotavirus A was the most detected virus (42.5%), followed by enterovirus (36%), human herpesvirus (HHV) (30%), adenovirus (25.5%), astrovirus (23.9%), and norovirus (22.7%). VCS detected a broader range of viral pathogens among the subset of 233 participant samples that were also tested using qPCR, with higher prevalence measurements for adenovirus (24.5% by VCS vs. 10.7% by qPCR) and norovirus (21.9% by VCS vs. 15.9% by qPCR) whereas rotavirus A and astrovirus showed comparable prevalence across both platforms. Age-specific trends revealed decreasing prevalence of rotavirus with increasing age, while adenovirus and enterovirus predominated in children aged > 24 months. No individual viral pathogen was significantly associated with diarrhea severity; however, rotavirus co-infections modified outcomes, with rotavirus-sapovirus associated with increased severity (aPR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.03–1.88, p = 0.029). Dual infections were common (31.9%), while mono-infections accounted for 38.5% of cases, and 8.9% had no detectable virus. VCS enables broad detection of pathogenic viruses, revealing diversity and co-infections in pediatric diarrheal disease. Expanded viral surveillance may improve pathogen detection, guide clinical management, reduce inappropriate antibiotic use, assess vaccine strategies, and strengthen disease control in high-burden settings.

papers.title_zh: VirCapSeq-VERT 在赞比亚五岁以下急性腹泻儿童病毒病原体检测中的应用
papers.source_body_en: Diarrheal disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five years, especially in low- and middle-income countries, particularly sub-Saharan Africa. Although rotavirus vaccination has reduced burden in children, a substantial proportion of diarrhea remains unattributed due to limited diagnostic capacity. We applied VirCapSeq-VERT (VCS), a virome-wide targeted sequencing technique, to characterize viral detections and co-infection patterns in stool samples from children with diarrhea and to explore their comparison with disease severity. A cross-sectional, facility-based study across nine provincial health facilities in Zambia. Stool collected from children U5 years presenting with diarrhea was analyzed using qPCR and VCS. Positivity by VCS was defined as ≥ 25% in relation to full coding reference sequence. Severity was assessed using the Vesikari scoring system and categorized as mild or moderate-to-severe. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to evaluate viral prevalence, age-specific distribution, and co-infection patterns. Samples from 247 participants were analyzed by VCS with 48.6% aged 0–12 months; males accounting for 52.6%. Using VCS to interrogate the stool samples, rotavirus A was the most detected virus (42.5%), followed by enterovirus (36%), human herpesvirus (HHV) (30%), adenovirus (25.5%), astrovirus (23.9%), and norovirus (22.7%). VCS detected a broader range of viral pathogens among the subset of 233 participant samples that were also tested using qPCR, with higher prevalence measurements for adenovirus (24.5% by VCS vs. 10.7% by qPCR) and norovirus (21.9% by VCS vs. 15.9% by qPCR) whereas rotavirus A and astrovirus showed comparable prevalence across both platforms. Age-specific trends revealed decreasing prevalence of rotavirus with increasing age, while adenovirus and enterovirus predominated in children aged > 24 months. No individual viral pathogen was significantly associated with diarrhea severity; however, rotavirus co-infections modified outcomes, with rotavirus-sapovirus associated with increased severity (aPR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.03–1.88, p = 0.029). Dual infections were common (31.9%), while mono-infections accounted for 38.5% of cases, and 8.9% had no detectable virus. VCS enables broad detection of pathogenic viruses, revealing diversity and co-infections in pediatric diarrheal disease. Expanded viral surveillance may improve pathogen detection, guide clinical management, reduce inappropriate antibiotic use, assess vaccine strategies, and strengthen disease control in high-burden settings.

papers.title: National trends in pathogen-specific diagnoses and outcomes among hospitalizations for infectious diarrhea.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The diagnostic evaluation of infectious diarrhea has evolved with increasing adoption of multiplex gastrointestinal nucleic acid amplification tests and changing diagnostic strategies for Clostridioides difficile. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to assess changes in inpatient pathogen-specific documentation rates and clinical outcomes on a national level. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cross-sectional study using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2023. Adult hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of presumed infectious diarrhea were identified using ICD-10 codes. Temporal trends in pathogen-specific documentation were evaluated. Multivariable regression models were used to identify factors associated with pathogen-specific documentation and evaluate associations with clinical outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 1,174,500 hospitalizations for presumed infectious diarrhea were identified, of which 710,335 (60.5%) had a specified pathogen. Pathogen specification rates remained stable from 2016 to 2023 (minimum of 59.6% in 2019 to the maximum of 62.1% in 2023; OR per year 1.00, 95% CI: 1.00-1.01, p = .282). Clostridioides difficile declined over time, accounting for 53.7% of infectious diarrhea hospitalizations in 2016 compared to 41.2% in 2023 (OR per year 0.94, p < .001). In contrast, norovirus and Campylobacter jejuni increased during the study period. Older age and higher comorbidity burden were independently associated with increased pathogen-specific documentation. Pathogen-specific documentation was associated with increased mortality (aOR 3.15, 95% CI: 2.73-3.63). These associations were substantially attenuated after exclusion of Clostridioides difficile. CONCLUSIONS: Pathogen-specific documentation rates among hospitalizations for presumed infectious diarrhea remained stable nationally from 2016 to 2023, although identification of non-Clostridioides difficile infections appeared to increase.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The diagnostic evaluation of infectious diarrhea has evolved with increasing adoption of multiplex gastrointestinal nucleic acid amplification tests and changing diagnostic strategies for Clostridioides difficile. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to assess changes in inpatient pathogen-specific documentation rates and clinical outcomes on a national level. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cross-sectional study using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2023. Adult hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of presumed infectious diarrhea were identified using ICD-10 codes. Temporal trends in pathogen-specific documentation were evaluated. Multivariable regression models were used to identify factors associated with pathogen-specific documentation and evaluate associations with clinical outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 1,174,500 hospitalizations for presumed infectious diarrhea were identified, of which 710,335 (60.5%) had a specified pathogen. Pathogen specification rates remained stable from 2016 to 2023 (minimum of 59.6% in 2019 to the maximum of 62.1% in 2023; OR per year 1.00, 95% CI: 1.00-1.01, p = .282). Clostridioides difficile declined over time, accounting for 53.7% of infectious diarrhea hospitalizations in 2016 compared to 41.2% in 2023 (OR per year 0.94, p < .001). In contrast, norovirus and Campylobacter jejuni increased during the study period. Older age and higher comorbidity burden were independently associated with increased pathogen-specific documentation. Pathogen-specific documentation was associated with increased mortality (aOR 3.15, 95% CI: 2.73-3.63). These associations were substantially attenuated after exclusion of Clostridioides difficile. CONCLUSIONS: Pathogen-specific documentation rates among hospitalizations for presumed infectious diarrhea remained stable nationally from 2016 to 2023, although identification of non-Clostridioides difficile infections appeared to increase.

papers.title: Evolution, diversity and distribution of human Noroviruses:From single hosts to global patterns
papers.abstract: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus causes substantial global morbidity and mortality from acute gastroenteritis, yet key knowledge gaps persist regarding its high diversity, within-host and community-level evolution, and links between diversity and treatment outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This thesis synthesizes existing evidence to address norovirus diversity and epidemiology across hosts and populations, integrating host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing for population-level monitoring.
analysis.methods: The study employs a comparative and integrative approach, combining literature review with wastewater-based sequencing to examine viral diversity and circulation patterns at the population level.
analysis.main_results: The thesis identifies over 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, with GII.4 continuously generating new antigenic variants, highlighting the virus's extensive diversity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work interprets the observed diversity as a driver of therapeutic challenges and proposes wastewater-based sequencing as a tool to monitor norovirus evolution and circulation, emphasizing the need to bridge within-host and community-level evolutionary insights.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance strategies and underscore the urgency for vaccine and antiviral development, given the absence of licensed options and the virus's antigenic variability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by its reliance on a literature-based synthesis and wastewater sequencing, which may not capture all host-specific dynamics or treatment associations, warranting moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis examines norovirus diversity and epidemiology to address critical gaps in understanding its evolution and public health impact. It synthesizes evidence showing norovirus as a major global cause of acute gastroenteritis, with over 10 genogroups and 50 genotypes, including the antigenically variable GII.4. The study integrates host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level. Key findings highlight the virus's extensive diversity as a barrier to therapeutic and vaccine development, with no licensed antivirals or vaccines currently available. The work interprets these patterns as evidence of ongoing antigenic drift and calls for improved surveillance and intervention strategies. Limitations include the reliance on literature synthesis and wastewater data, which may not fully capture host-specific dynamics or treatment outcomes, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.title: Molecular Detection of Gastrointestinal Pathogens Using a Multiplex Gastrointestinal Panel and Their Associations With Demographic and Clinical Characteristics
papers.abstract: BackgroundAcute gastroenteritis causes morbidity across all age groups, and timely, effective identification of its etiologic agents is essential for clinical management and antimicrobial stewardship.Conventional diagnostic methods have limited sensitivity and often fail to detect coinfections or specific bacterial pathotypes.In contrast, molecular methods, such as FilmArray panels, are rapid, highly sensitive, and capable of detecting coinfections.This study aimed to characterize gastrointestinal pathogens detected by the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BioFire Diagnostics, LLC, Salt Lake City, UT, USA; a bioMérieux company) and to evaluate their association with demographic and clinical characteristics among patients at Hospital Angeles Lindavista, Mexico City, Mexico. MethodsA retrospective observational study conducted from January 2022 to July 2025 included all patients who underwent gastrointestinal molecular testing.Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and multiplex PCR results were extracted from electronic medical records and the FilmArray database.Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, logistic regression, Fisher's exact test, and Spearman correlation. ResultsAn analysis of 1,120 samples found an overall positivity rate of 906 (81%).Coinfections were present in 543 (49%) cases.The most common pathogens were enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (E.coli, EPEC; 374, 33.4%); enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC; 281, 25.1%); and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC; 231, 20.6%).Rotavirus A (206, 18.4%) and norovirus GI/GII (168, 15%) were the most frequent.Positivity was highest in children under five (147, 84.48%) and lowest in adults over 60 (129, 73.71%).Seasonal patterns showed unexpected peaks of rotavirus in spring-summer and of Cyclospora cayetanensis in summer.No significant association was found between pathogen presence and comorbidities, likely due to many missing clinical details.A negative correlation among major E. coli pathotypes suggests competitive exclusion. ConclusionThe BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel identified pathogen patterns that conventional methods miss.Age and seasonal trends highlight the need for localized epidemiological surveillance.These results encourage the use of molecular diagnostics in routine assessments of gastrointestinal infections and support antimicrobial stewardship efforts.Future studies should include clinical severity metrics and evaluate patient outcomes to connect molecular detection with clinical significance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to characterize gastrointestinal pathogens detected by the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel and to evaluate their association with demographic and clinical characteristics among patients at Hospital Angeles Lindavista, Mexico City, Mexico.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective observational study conducted from January 2022 to July 2025 included all patients who underwent gastrointestinal molecular testing. The study population comprised 1,120 samples, with a positivity rate of 906 (81%) for various pathogens.
analysis.methods: Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and multiplex PCR results were extracted from electronic medical records and the FilmArray database. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, logistic regression, Fisher's exact test, and Spearman correlation.
analysis.main_results: An analysis of 1,120 samples found an overall positivity rate of 906 (81%). Coinfections were present in 543 (49%) cases. The most common pathogens were enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC; 374, 33.4%), enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC; 281, 25.1%), and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC; 231, 20.6%). Rotavirus A (206, 18.4%) and norovirus GI/GII (168, 15%) were the most frequent. Positivity was highest in children under five (147, 84.48%) and lowest in adults over 60 (129, 73.71%). Seasonal patterns showed unexpected peaks of rotavirus in spring-summer and of Cyclospora cayetanensis in summer. No significant association was found between pathogen presence and comorbidities, likely due to many missing clinical details.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of molecular diagnostics in identifying pathogens that conventional methods may miss, particularly in detecting coinfections and specific bacterial pathotypes. The negative correlation among major E. coli pathotypes suggests competitive exclusion.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of molecular diagnostics in routine assessments of gastrointestinal infections and emphasize the need for localized epidemiological surveillance, especially in identifying age-specific and seasonal trends in norovirus and other pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the lack of significant association between pathogen presence and comorbidities, likely due to many missing clinical details. The evidence is moderate, as the study is observational and relies on existing medical records.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel to detect gastrointestinal pathogens and their associations with demographic and clinical characteristics at Hospital Angeles Lindavista in Mexico City. The analysis of 1,120 samples revealed an overall positivity rate of 81%, with coinfections present in 49% of cases. Norovirus GI/GII and Rotavirus A were the most frequently detected pathogens, with higher positivity rates in children under five and unexpected seasonal peaks. The study found no significant association between pathogen presence and comorbidities, possibly due to incomplete clinical data. These results underscore the value of molecular diagnostics in identifying pathogens missed by conventional methods and highlight the need for localized surveillance. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and reliance on existing records.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2022年1月至2025年7月进行的一项回顾性观察研究包括所有接受胃肠道分子检测的患者。研究人群包括 1,120 个样本,各种病原体的阳性率为 906 例(81%)。
elements_zh.methods: 从电子病历和 FilmArray 数据库中提取人口统计数据、临床特征和多重 PCR 结果。使用描述性统计、逻辑回归、Fisher 精确检验和 Spearman 相关性对数据进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: An analysis of 1,120 samples found an overall positivity rate of 906 (81%). Coinfections were present in 543 (49%) cases. The most common pathogens were enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC; 374, 33.4%), enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC; 281, 25.1%), and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC; 231, 20.6%). Rotavirus A (206, 18.4%) and norovirus GI/GII (168, 15%) were the most frequent. Positivity was highest in children under five (147, 84.48%) and lowest in adults over 60 (129, 73.71%). Seasonal patterns showed unexpected peaks of rotavirus in spring-summer and of Cyclospora cayetanensis in summer. No significant association was found between pathogen presence and comorbidities, likely due to many missing clinical details.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了分子诊断在识别传统方法可能遗漏的病原体方面的重要性,特别是在检测合并感染和特定细菌致病型方面。主要大肠杆菌致病型之间的负相关表明竞争排斥。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在胃肠道感染的常规评估中使用分子诊断,并强调对局部流行病学 监测 的需求,特别是在识别 诺如病毒 和其他病原体的年龄特异性和季节性趋势方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括病原体存在与合并症之间缺乏显着关联,这可能是由于许多临床细节缺失所致。证据是中等的,因为该研究是观察性的并且依赖于现有的医疗记录。

media_mentions.content: The BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel identified pathogen patterns that conventional methods miss. Age and seasonal trends highlight the need for localized epidemiological surveillance. These results encourage the use of molecular diagnostics in routine assessments of gastrointestinal infections and support antimicrobial stewardship efforts. Future studies should include clinical severity metrics and evaluate patient outcomes to connect molecular detection with clinical significance. An analysis of 1,120 samples found an overall positivity rate of 906 (81%). Coinfections were present in 543 (49%) cases. The most common pathogens were enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (E. coli, EPEC; 374, 33.4%); enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC; 281, 25.1%); and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC; 231, 20.6%). Rotavirus A (206, 18.4%) and norovirus GI/GII (168, 15%) were the most frequent. Positivity was highest in children under five (147, 84.48%) and lowest in adults over 60 (129, 73.71%). Seasonal patterns showed unexpected peaks of rotavirus in spring-summer and of Cyclospora cayetanensis in summer. No significant association was found between pathogen presence and comorbidities, likely due to many missing clinical details. A negative correlation among major E. coli pathotypes suggests competitive exclusion. A retrospective observational study conducted from January 2022 to July 2025 included all patients who underwent gastrointestinal molecular testing. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and multiplex PCR results were extracted from electronic medical records and the FilmArray database. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, logistic regression, Fisher’s exact test, and Spearman correlation. Acute gastroenteritis causes morbidity across all age groups, and timely, effective identification of its etiologic agents is essential for clinical management and antimicrobial stewardship. Conventional diagnostic methods have limited sensitivity and often fail to detect coinfections or specific bacterial pathotypes. In contrast, molecular methods, such as FilmArray panels, are rapid, highly sensitive, and capable of detecting coinfections. This study aimed to characterize gastrointestinal pathogens detected by the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BioFire Diagnostics, LLC, Salt Lake City, UT, USA; a bioMérieux company) and to evaluate their association with demographic and clinical characteristics among patients at Hospital Angeles Lindavista, Mexico City, Mexico. Introduction Gastrointestinal infections are a common reason for seeking medical care and a global public health problem. While pediatric patients are known to be the most vulnerable, these infections also represent a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in adults, particularly those with comorbidities [1,2]. Rapid, timely diagnosis improves treatment, disease course, and prognosis and supports epidemiological surveillance. One of the greatest challenges in establishing a diagnosis is the wide range of pathogens that can cause infection, including viruses, bacteria, and parasites, acting alone or in combination [3]. Current diagnostic testing options include culture, staining, and antigen detection. These methods may require collecting multiple samples, involve extensive sample preparation, and have low sensitivity and prolonged turnaround times. Traditionally, the gold standard for microbiological diagnosis includes culture for Salmonella spp., Shigella spp., Campylobacter, and Escherichia coli (E. coli), as well as rapid tests for rotavirus. However, these agents account for only 25%-30% of diarrheal syndromes [4]. Molecular detection tests have expanded the capacity to detect pathogens. However, their availability is limited for most of the population due to their high cost and limited access in public health institutions [5]. For the FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has validated its clinical use, allowing detection in a single reaction of 22 enteric pathogens (13 bacteria, five viruses, and four parasites) and resistance genes [6]. In Mexico, this technique is not widely available in public health services and is used only in specific cases or in the private sector [7]. Therefore, describing its use in the general population is relevant, as is its association with clinical characteristics such as diagnosis, comorbidities, and risk factors. This study aims to identify and describe the microorganisms detected in patients who underwent a gastrointestinal molecular panel at Hospital Ángeles Lindavista, Mexico City, Mexico, from January 2022 to July 2025, without establishing a definitive cause-and-effect relationship, and to evaluate their correlation with demographic and clinical features. To this end, we will conduct a retrospective, descriptive analysis, with the results intended to inform improvements in patient care, diagnosis, treatment, antimicrobial stewardship decisions, and epidemiological surveillance. Materials & Methods Study design We conducted a retrospective, observational, cross-sectional study at Hospital Angeles Lindavista from January 2022 to July 2025. Its goal was to identify and examine gastrointestinal pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and parasites, detected by the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BioFire Diagnostics, LLC, Salt Lake City, UT, USA; a bioMérieux company). The study aimed not only to understand epidemiological patterns but also to associate these pathogens with patients' demographic and clinical features; it included all patients who received a gastrointestinal molecular panel, whether as outpatients or while hospitalized. Analyzed variables included demographics, patient type, comorbidities, risk factors, diagnoses, detected pathogens, and infection type. Data sources included the FilmArray multiplex PCR system database (by bioMérieux) and the Hospital Angeles Lindavista Electronic Clinical History (ECH) database. Laboratory testing Samples examined were stool specimens. We identified gastrointestinal pathogens using the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel multiplex PCR system. This certified device combines nucleic acid extraction, reverse transcription, first-stage multiplex PCR, and second-stage nested PCR within a single disposable pouch. It employs freeze-dried reagents and multiple primers optimized for a common annealing temperature, allowing simultaneous qualitative detection of 22 gastrointestinal pathogens, such as diarrheagenic E. coli types, Campylobacter, Salmonella, Vibrio, Yersinia enterocolitica, Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile) toxin A/B, Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia, adenovirus F40/41, astrovirus, norovirus GI/GII, rotavirus A, and sapovirus. All steps occur inside sealed blister compartments in the pouch, reducing manual handling and contamination risk and delivering results in about an hour. We performed tests following the manufacturer's protocols. Results labeled "detected" or "not detected" were considered valid. If a process failed, we marked the result "invalid" and repeated the test. This approach improves diagnostic speed and helps detect coinfections but has limitations: sensitivity varies among targets; it does not quantify microbial load, so it cannot differentiate active infection from colonization or residual nucleic acids, and it detects only organisms within the panel and cannot identify pathogens outside it. A negative result does not rule out microorganisms not among the panel's targets. Therefore, we interpreted results alongside clinical presentation and additional diagnostics. Data source We compiled a retrospective database from Hospital Angeles Lindavista for the specified period, including data from 1,120 patients. We de-identified the patients' data and standardized and grouped variable coding for analysis. Statistical analysis Statistical analyses were conducted using R version 4.5.1 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria) in RStudio (Posit Software, PBC, Boston, MA, USA). Descriptive Analysis Categorical variables were summarized with their absolute counts and percentages. For the continuous variable (age), we assessed the data distribution and reported the mean and standard deviation (SD). Overall and age-specific positivity rates were calculated by dividing detected cases by the total samples processed. Seasonality Analysis We examined the monthly detection frequency of the top 10 most common pathogens over the study period (2022-2025) to identify seasonal trends and periodic fluctuations. Inferential Analysis and Associations To analyze links between clinical variables (such as comorbidities and risk factors) and pathogen presence, we used binary logistic regression to calculate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For small subgroups (n < 5), we used Fisher's exact test for sensitivity checks. Finally, to investigate microbial interactions (coinfections versus mutual exclusion), we created a correlation matrix based on Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, considering only statistically significant interactions. All statistical tests used a significance threshold of p < 0.05 (two-tailed). Ethical considerations The Research Ethics Committee of Hospital Angeles Pedregal approved the study protocol (approval number: HAP 2786). All procedures followed the ethical standards outlined in the Declaration of Helsinki. The committee granted a waiver of informed consent for this retrospective study because of its minimal-risk design. Confidentiality and data protection were maintained throughout the study. Results Characteristics of the study population A total of 1,120 samples from patients with suspected gastrointestinal infection treated at Hospital Angeles Lindavista between January 2022 and July 2025 were analyzed. The mean age of the patients was 33.6 years (SD ± 23.1). A balanced gender distribution was observed, with 616 (55%) female patients. Most samples (1,028, 92%) were from hospitalized patients, while 92 (8%) were from outpatients (Table 1). Characteristic N = 1,120 Age (years) 34 (23) Age group Children (0–5 years) 174 (16%) Children (6–17 years) 152 (14%) Adults (18–59 years) 619 (55%) Older adults (>60 years) 175 (16%) Gender Female 616 (55%) Male 504 (45%) Patient type Outpatient 92 (8.2%) Hospitalized 1,028 (92%) Table 1: Clinical and demographic characteristics of the study population. For the age variable, the values correspond to the mean and standard deviation (SD). For the other values, these correspond to the number of cases (n) and the percentage of the total population (%). Regarding the diagnosis, 878 (79%) patients were admitted with acute gastroenteritis, 74 (6.6%) with gastroenteritis secondary to C. difficile, and 28 (2.5%) had no reported diagnosis. In 761 (68%) and 709 (64%) of the analyzed population, the presence of comorbidities and risk factors was unknown, respectively. Among patients with available information, hypertension (48, 4.3%) and diabetes (41, 3.7%) were the most frequent comorbidities, while immunosuppression (27, 2.4%) and the presence of concomitant infections (15, 1.3%) were among the most common risk factors (Table 2). Characteristic N = 1,120 Admission diagnosis Acute gastroenteritis 878 (79%) Gastroenteritis secondary to Clostridioides difficile 74 (6.6%) Other (postoperative, oncologic, neurologic, etc.) 49 (4.4%) No diagnosis 28 (2.5%) Abdominal and/or urinary sepsis 22 (2.0%) Urinary tract infection 21 (1.9%) Respiratory tract infection 13 (1.2%) Unspecified gastropathy 12 (1.1%) Unknown 9 (0.8%) Infectious colitis 7 (0.6%) Inflammatory bowel disease/Crohn’s disease -ulcerative colitis 4 (0.4%) Comorbidities Unknown 761 (68%) None 191 (17%) Hypertension 48 (4.3%) Diabetes 41 (3.7%) Cancer 21 (1.9%) Chronic kidney disease 18 (1.6%) Other (neurologic, respiratory, rheumatologic, etc.) 13 (1.2%) Hypothyroidism 11 (1.0%) Heart failure 9 (0.8%) Unspecified gastropathy 4 (0.4%) Liver failure 3 (0.3%) Risk factors Unknown 709 (64%) None 281 (25%) Other (diabetes, hypertension, Parkinson’s disease) 28 (2.5%) Immunosuppression 27 (2.4%) Concomitant infection 15 (1.3%) Poor diet 11 (1.0%) Short breastfeeding duration 11 (1.0%) Post-surgical 10 (0.9%) Renal failure 10 (0.9%) Hypothyroidism 5 (0.4%) Irritable bowel syndrome 5 (0.4%) HIV 4 (0.4%) Table 2: Admission diagnoses, comorbidities, and risk factors among patients. Each pair of data points corresponds to the number of cases (n) and the percentage of the total population (%). Prevalence and profile of gastrointestinal pathogens The overall positivity rate for the panel was 906 (81%). Among positive cases, coinfections were common: 363 (32%) had single infections (one pathogen), while 543 (49%) had multiple infections (two, three, or more than four pathogens detected simultaneously) (Table 3). Characteristic N = 1,120 Gastrointestinal panel result Detected (positive) 906 (81%) Not detected (negative) 214 (19%) Classification by number of pathogens No infection 214 (19%) Single infection (1 pathogen) 363 (32%) Double infection (2 pathogens) 258 (23%) Triple infection (3 pathogens) 166 (15%) Multiple infections (>4 pathogens) 119 (11%) Table 3: Gastrointestinal panel results and infection burden in the study population. Each pair of data points corresponds to the number of cases (n) and the percentage of the total population (%). Pathogenic bacteria dominated the microbiological profile. The most frequently detected microorganisms were enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), 374 (33.4%), followed by enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC), 281 (25.1%), and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC), 231 (20.6%). Among viral agents, rotavirus A was most prevalent (206, 18.4%), followed by norovirus GI/GII (168, 15%) (Figure 1). Figure 1: Frequency of enteric pathogens identified through a multiplex gastrointestinal panel. Each horizontal bar represents a pathogen, showing detection rates and counts. The data primarily indicate that Escherichia coli (E. coli) pathotypes dominate. Viral pathogens such as rotavirus A and norovirus GI/GII are also notably present. Less common are E. coli O157 at 18(1.61%) and Cryptosporidium spp. at 16(1.43%). Overall, the figure illustrates pathogen burden and relative frequencies within the study group. By age group, the molecular panel showed high detection rates (>73%) across all groups (Figure 2). Nevertheless, positivity declined with age: children aged 0 to five years had the highest rate at 147/174 (84.48%), closely followed by the six-to 17-year group at 128/152 (84.21%). Conversely, adults over 60 years had the lowest detection rate at 129/175 (73.71%), suggesting a potentially higher prevalence of non-infectious or undetectable causes in this age group. Figure 2: Gastrointestinal panel positivity rate stratified by age group. The highest positivity rates are observed in children aged 0 to five years. Adults aged 18 to 59 show a slightly lower rate of 502/619 (81.1%), while those over 60 have the lowest rate at 129/175 (73.71%). These data suggest that positivity decreases with age, highlighting age-related differences in detecting the pathogen. Seasonality patterns Monthly trend analysis revealed seasonal patterns (Figure 3). Unlike the common winter peaks seen elsewhere, rotavirus detections surged in spring and summer (March-June), aligning with peaks in bacterial pathogens such as Salmonella spp. and various E. coli strains. Furthermore, C. difficile cases peaked from May to July. Cyclospora cayetanensis also showed a distinct summer seasonal pattern. Figure 3: Monthly distribution of cases for multiple gastrointestinal pathogens. A seasonal pattern trend appears, with most pathogen cases increasing from April to July. The highest peaks are observed among Escherichia coli (E. coli) pathotypes, namely enteropathogenic E. coli (EPEC), enteroaggregative E. coli (EAEC), and enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC), with counts approaching 60 in late spring and early summer. Other pathogens such as Campylobacter spp., Salmonella spp., Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), and enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC) also exhibit a similar seasonal rise, though less pronounced. After July, case counts decline sharply and remain low for the rest of the year. Overall, the data highlight a distinct mid-year surge in enteric infections, consistent with typical seasonal epidemiological patterns. Association with age group Multivariate analysis showed a strong association between age and infection etiology (Figure 4). Compared with the adult group (18 to 59 years), pediatric patients (0 to five years) had a significantly higher probability of infection with viral agents, notably rotavirus (OR > 1, p < 0.05) and norovirus. This age group also had a higher probability of detecting bacteria such as C. difficile and Campylobacter spp. Other pathogens, such as EPEC and ETEC, were less likely to be isolated in children aged 0 to five years, and Cyclospora cayetanensis was less likely to be isolated in pediatric patients overall. Furthermore, C. difficile showed a trend towards higher detection in adults over 60 years of age, consistent with the hospital epidemiology of this pathogen. Figure 4: Comparative analysis of infection risk across age groups using odds ratios on a logarithmic scale. Three panels present the relative odds of pathogen detection among adults aged 60 and over, children aged 0 to five, and children aged six to 17, each compared with adults aged 18 to 59. The chart displays point estimates with CIs for different pathogens, using red markers to indicate statistically significant associations (p<0.05) and gray markers for non-significant results. It highlights age-related variations in susceptibility, showing which pathogens are more or less commonly detected in younger children and older adults compared with the adult reference group. news.content: 正体 新闻 中国 评论 文化 生活 娱乐 健康 体育 社区 神韵 国际要闻 古巴腹泻病例激增 美使馆发布旅行健康警示 更新: 2026年09月07日 1:17 PM 图为示意图。美囯驻古巴大使馆。(YAMIL LAGE/AFP/Getty Images) 【大纪元2026年09月07日讯】(英文大纪元记者Jacki Thrapp撰文/高杉编译)美国驻古巴大使馆(U.S. Embassy in Cuba)9月4日发布旅行健康警示,提醒已经或计划前往古巴的美国民众注意,该国供水及电网系统的崩溃,正导致肠胃疾病大幅增加。 民众应注意饮食卫生 美国大使馆指出,随着水利及能源基础设施状况持续恶化,古巴各地腹泻性疾病病例显着增多。基础设施恶化已波及供水系统、食品储存及温度控制,进而引发大肠杆菌(E. coli)、诺如病毒(norovirus)、志贺氏菌(Shigella)等肠胃道病原体感染率增加。 大使馆敦促已在古巴的美国民众,对未妥善储存的肉类、禽肉、海鲜、鸡蛋、乳制品及其它易腐食品保持谨慎态度。 大使馆建议,应避免食用长时间置于室温下的食物,避免生食或食用未彻底清洗的蔬菜,并在食用经冷却后重新加热的熟食前多加留意。 同时建议勤洗手,保持充足水分摄入。如果出现持续性或严重腹泻、血便、高烧、明显腹痛、反复呕吐、脱水迹象,或症状未见好转,应及时就医。 供水与停电问题加剧 8月28日,美国大使馆官员也曾发布警告说,古巴供水基础设施日趋不稳定,部分社区反映,当地已长时间停止供水。往往只有当城市供电时间足够长时,住宅才能获得供水。 美国大使馆官员指出,供水问题及停电现象,是由于古巴共产主义政权对全岛公共基础设施管理不善所致。 原文:US Embassy Issues Health Alert for Cuba After ‘Significant Increase in Diarrheal Illness’ 刊登于英文《大纪元时报》 责任编辑:李沐恩# 浏览大纪元网页 标签 旅行 健康 美国 古巴,大使馆 腹泻 捐助大纪元 人人有 ‘好报’ 相关文章 古巴男子被控伪造医疗证明 助14人免试入美籍 美破获跨国偷渡网 古巴男子助数千人非法入美 美国宣布新制裁 锁定古巴颠覆性反美网络 美国宣布制裁古巴党魁卡斯特罗之孙 匈牙利驱逐10名俄外交官 俄扬言将报复 美孤立德黑兰最新行动 全面制裁伊朗航空业 【直播】卢比奥会哥国总统签署核能关键矿产约 EUV光刻机订单排满 ASML大规模扩建荷兰工厂 【军事情报局】伊朗弹道飞弹 突袭美航母失败 回应美舰遭袭 美军摧毁伊朗五艘油轮

supplementary_news.content_title: Luxury hotel to reopen on Thursday following recent norovirus outbreak
supplementary_news.content: A luxury Co Westmeath hotel that had to temporarily close following a norovirus outbreak last month is due to reopen on Thursday. Glasson Lakehouse, a four-star hotel located 13km from Athlone, closed on August 26th following advice from the HSE . Four couples due to celebrate their weddings at the hotel in the last two weeks had to find alternative venues , including a couple from Galway who managed to rearrange their plans in just a few hours . A spokeswoman for Glasson Lakehouse said the hotel would reopen on Thursday, with weddings due to take place there this weekend. READ MORE ‘Tipping point’: Why are people giving up their health insurance? NI has highest infant mortality rate in UK, paediatricians warn Palliative care: How treatment for four-year-old Eva led to her ‘living her happy life’ ‘People come to our exercise classes with heart disease, lung disease, cancer, diabetes’ Norovirus, which causes diarrhoea and vomiting, is one of the most common stomach bugs. It is understood that a significant number of guests and staff at the hotel were impacted by the virus last month. The spokeswoman previously said hotel management “deeply” regretted the inconvenience caused by the outbreak and thanked guests for their patience. [ From devastation to pure love: Couple finds venue after hotel closes two days before wedding Opens in new window ] The HSE last week said it had “provided comprehensive public health and environmental health advice, information and support to assist the premises in developing and reviewing its reopening plans”. “While the HSE can provide expert guidance on risk management measures, the decision to reopen is a matter for the premises management team following its own assessment of the risks and operational considerations,” it said in a statement. Careful food handling and hand hygiene help prevent the spread of norovirus, the HSE said. People who are unwell with norovirus should stay off work or school until they have been symptom free for 48 hours
